bull_bear.body:

- Highly competitive and fragmented market — The Indian pharmaceutical industry is highly fragmented with over 10,000 manufacturers in the organised and unorganised sectors, and approximately 8,000 SMEs make up about 70% of total pharmaceutical units. Some competitors may have substantially greater financial, marketing, technical or other resources; competition may decrease the price paid for the Company's products and services.

- Single manufacturing location — Manufacturing is situated at one site at Palghar, Maharashtra (Unit 1, with Unit 2 being added at the same existing facility), concentrating operational, regulatory and licensing exposure at one location.
- Unit 2 commissioning and licensing execution — Unit 2 has been constructed and an application has been made for the required licenses, but it is under commissioning and production is yet to commence, so the stated incremental annual capacity is not yet operating.
- Planned international expansion introduces new competitive and execution exposure — The Company states that as it commences international business it expects competition from major international generic manufacturers, and flags that failure to manage the risks associated with exporting products internationally may adversely affect business, results of operations, financial condition and future prospects.

outlook.body:
- Revenue concentration in tender-based sales to Government Customers (approximately 90% of revenue from operations across the reported periods), so revenue depends on acceptance of bids submitted in competitive procurement processes
- Lengthening working capital cycle - Net Working Capital Days rose from 52 in Fiscal 2023 to 78 in Fiscal 2024, 115 in Fiscal 2025 and 133 in the six months ended September 30, 2025
- Receivables extension - Debtor Days of 97 (Fiscal 2023), 92 (Fiscal 2024), 97 (Fiscal 2025) and 124 in the six months ended September 30, 2025; Creditor Days compressed from 52 (Fiscal 2023) to 20 (Fiscal 2025) and 26 in the six months ended September 30, 2025
- Margin expansion - EBITDA margin moved from 17.81% in Fiscal 2023 to 23.66% in Fiscal 2024 and 24.52% in Fiscal 2025, with 22.60% in the six months ended September 30, 2025; PAT margin moved from 12.91% to 18.78% over Fiscal 2023 to Fiscal 2025
- Therapeutic mix shift - Antiparasitic fell from 13.06% of revenue in Fiscal 2023 to 0.08% in the six months ended September 30, 2025 while Blood Related rose to 22.70% and Keratolytic rose from 2.98% to 6.67% over the same span
- Emerging private-customer channel - private customer revenue rose from 0.21% of revenue in Fiscal 2023 to 9.17% in Fiscal 2025 and 10.07% in the six months ended September 30, 2025
- Low leverage - Debt/Equity of 0.01 (Fiscal 2023), 0.08 (Fiscal 2024), 0.06 (Fiscal 2025) and 0.04 at the six months ended September 30, 2025
- Competition and pricing - the Company competes on product portfolio, quality and regulatory compliance, on-time delivery and manufacturing flexibility, and cost-effective manufacturing; competition may result in a decrease in the price paid for its products and services

business_ops.seasonality: The DRHP discloses no company-level seasonality of revenue or production; its revenue is tender-driven business-to-government supply. The industry section (CareEdge Report) notes seasonal demand drivers in therapeutic segments the Company sells into - seasonal outbreaks and rising fungal infections keeping anti-infective demand high through the year, and rising air pollution, tobacco use and seasonal infections supporting respiratory drug demand.
business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Integrated formulation manufacturing at a single Palghar site: the Company manufactures multiple dosage forms (tablets, capsules, sachets, bottles, external liquids, creams, aerosols, ointments, combination blister packages and external powders) in-house, and describes a versatile facility able to produce multiple products using a combination of processes, allowing the product mix to be changed in response to changes in market demand. Quality control is in-house: the quality control department has the responsibility and authority to approve or reject raw materials, packaging components, intermediate materials, in-process materials, semi-finished products and finished products. Inputs are bought in rather than backward-integrated; cost of material consumed (raw materials plus packing materials) was 48.15% of total expenses in the six months ended September 30, 2025 and 51.79%, 51.83% and 57.03% of total expenses in Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023. The Company states it has no long-term contracts with its third-party suppliers; prices are negotiated for each purchase order and it generally has more than one supplier for each raw material. It also purchases stock-in-trade (trading goods purchases of Rs 110.43 million in the six months ended September 30, 2025 and Rs 194.45 million and Rs 33.43 million in Fiscals 2025 and 2024). Downstream, the Palghar facility is equipped with a warehouse; products are sold on a Cost and Freight (CnF) basis; the Company owns no vehicles for transportation and relies on third-party transportation and logistics providers, with finished goods shipped through freight forwarders appointed by the Company or nominated by customers. Freight charges were 2.43% of total expenses in the six months ended September 30, 2025 and 2.93%, 2.78% and 2.48% in Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023. Route to market is direct tender-based supply to Government Customers, handled by a dedicated tendering team of 8 personnel as of September 30, 2025; no distributor or retail channel layer is described.

overview.business_model: The company manufactures generic formulations (medicines whose patents have expired, typically used as substitutes for more expensive branded medicines) at its Palghar, Maharashtra facility and supplies them primarily under procurement contracts won through competitive government tenders. Customers are central government projects under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare via GoI agencies, plus state government agencies and bodies (together, Government Customers), alongside a smaller private-customer stream. Products are supplied either under brand names or under generic names depending on customer requirements, and all products (other than those manufactured for others) carry the company's logo. Government Customers contributed 89.93% of revenue from operations in the six months ended September 30, 2025, 90.83% in Fiscal 2025, 98.14% in Fiscal 2024 and 99.79% in Fiscal 2023. Products were supplied to 27 States and Union Territories during the six months ended September 30, 2025 and to 27 States and Union Territories during Fiscal 2025.

compliance_legal.detail: The healthcare industry is subject to reform, adverse changes in government or private funding of healthcare products and services, and legislation or regulations governing pricing or reimbursement of pharmaceuticals and mandated benefits. Indian pharmaceutical companies participating in business-to-government procurement operate under the CDSCO and the Drug Price Control Order framework enforced by the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority. If the prices of more of the Company's products or its customers' products are administered or determined by the DPCO, NPPA or similar authorities, it would have an adverse impact on profitability.
compliance_legal.evidence: "Every year on April 1, ceiling prices for over 923 scheduled formulations are adjusted based on the Wholesale Price Index (WPI). In 2024, the adjustment was negligible, and a modest hike is permitted from April 1, 2025, both reflecting minimal pricing flexibility even in the face of cost inflation. In 2019, NPPA imposed a 30% trade-margin cap on 42 non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs, which led to price reductions across 105 brands. (Source: CareEdge Report)"
compliance_legal.title: Healthcare reform, pharmaceutical pricing regulation and government price ceilings

compliance_legal.detail: There have been instances of delays, clerical errors, factual errors and non-compliance in corporate records. There was also a delay in transferring unspent CSR amounts within the stipulated 30 days for financial year 2022-23, and the Company did not file Form CRA-2 and Form CRA-4 in respect of the cost auditor appointment and cost audit report within prescribed timelines for financial years 2022, 2023 and 2024.

"the Company has filed adjudication applications in Form GNL-1 bearing SRN No. AC0216592 dated December 21, 2025, before the Registrar of Companies, Maharashtra at Mumbai ... under Section 443 of the Companies Act, 2013, for adjudication of non-compliance with the provisions of Section 149(4)". "As on the date of this Draft Red Herring Prospectus, the Company has not received any notice, order or communication from the Registrar in this regard."

compliance_legal.detail: The Competition Act, 2002 regulates practices having an appreciable adverse effect on competition in the relevant market in India. Agreements among competitors involving determination of purchase or sale prices, limits on production or supply, market sharing, or that directly or indirectly result in bid-rigging or collusive bidding are presumed to have an AAEC and are void. The Competition (Amendment) Act, 2023 gives the CCI additional powers and empowers it to impose penalties based on the global turnover of entities. The CCI has extraterritorial powers.
compliance_legal.evidence: "On April 11, 2023, the Competition (Amendment) Bill 2023 received the assent of the President of India to become the Competition (Amendment) Act, 2023"; "empowers the CCI to impose penalties based on the global turnover of entities, for anti-competitive agreements and abuse of dominant position."
compliance_legal.title: Application or interpretation of Indian competition law

compliance_legal.detail: The Company is incorporated under the laws of India, its Board comprises Indian citizens, all its assets are located in India, and its Key Managerial Personnel and Senior Management are residents of India with most of their assets in India. India has reciprocal recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters with only a limited number of jurisdictions, including the United Kingdom, Singapore, United Arab Emirates and Hong Kong. A judgment from a non-reciprocating territory cannot be executed in India and would require a new suit in a competent Indian court within three years.
compliance_legal.evidence: "Judgments or decrees from jurisdictions, which do not have reciprocal recognition with India, cannot be executed in India."; enforcement of a foreign judgment requires prior approval of the RBI to repatriate any amount recovered.
compliance_legal.title: Investors may not be able to enforce a judgment of a foreign court

compliance_legal.detail: Capital gains arising from the sale of equity shares held as investments in an Indian company are generally taxable in India unless specifically exempted, and securities transaction tax is levied and collected by the domestic stock exchange. Gains on listed shares held for more than 12 months are subject to long term capital gains tax at specified rates, and gains on shares held for 12 months or less are subject to short term capital gains tax. Under the Finance Act, 2020, dividend distribution tax is not payable on dividends declared, distributed or paid after March 31, 2020, and such dividends are not exempt in the hands of shareholders and are subject to tax deduction at source. The impact of amendments introduced by the Finance Act, 2024 has not been fully determined.
compliance_legal.evidence: "The stamp duty for transfer of securities other than debentures, on a delivery basis is specified at 0.015% and on a non-delivery basis is specified at 0.003% of the consideration amount. These amendments have come into effect from July 1, 2020."; "We have not fully determined the impact of these recent and proposed laws and regulations on our business, results of operations, cash flows and financial condition."
compliance_legal.title: Indian taxes on income arising from sale of and dividend on the Equity Shares

compliance_legal.detail: Foreign ownership of Indian securities is subject to Government regulation. Transfers of shares between non-residents and residents are freely permitted subject to compliance with sectoral norms and pricing guidelines and reporting requirements specified by the RBI, failing which prior RBI approval is required. Shareholders seeking to convert Indian Rupee proceeds from a sale of shares into foreign currency and repatriate it require a no objection or tax clearance certificate from the Indian income tax authority. Under Press Note No. 3 (2020 Series) dated April 17, 2020 and the Foreign Exchange Management (Non-debt Instruments) Amendment Rules, 2020 effective April 22, 2020, investment by entities of a country sharing a land border with India, or where the beneficial owner is situated in or is a citizen of such a country, can only be made through the Government approval route, and these restrictions also apply to subscribers of offshore derivative instruments.
compliance_legal.evidence: "pursuant to Press Note No. 3 (2020 Series), dated April 17, 2020 issued by the DPIIT and the Foreign Exchange Management (Non-debt Instruments) Amendment Rules, 2020 which came into effect from April 22, 2020".
compliance_legal.title: Foreign investment restrictions under Indian laws

financial_valuation.detail: The Offer consists of a Fresh Issue and an Offer for Sale. The Selling Shareholder is entitled to the net proceeds from the Offer for Sale, comprising proceeds net of Offer expenses shared by the Selling Shareholder, and the Company will not receive any proceeds from the Offer for Sale.

financial_valuation.title: No proceeds from the Offer for Sale accrue to the Company

financial_valuation.detail: Performance and growth depend on the health of the overall Indian economy. Any slowdown or perceived slowdown in the Indian economy or Indian pharmaceutical industry and volatility in interest rates could materially and adversely affect the business. An increase in trade deficit or a decline in India's foreign exchange reserves could negatively affect liquidity. A slowdown could also adversely affect Government of India policy towards the pharmaceutical industry.
financial_valuation.evidence: "India's economy could be adversely affected by a general rise in interest rates or inflation, adverse weather conditions affecting agriculture, commodity and energy prices as well as various other factors like global pandemics."
financial_valuation.title: Slowdown in economic growth in India

financial_valuation.detail: Inflation rates in India have been volatile in recent years. Increased inflation can contribute to an increase in interest rates and increased costs including transportation, wages, raw materials and other expenses, and high fluctuations in inflation rates may make it more difficult to accurately estimate or control costs. Increased inflation may not be adequately passed on to customers, whether entirely or in part.
financial_valuation.evidence: "If inflation were to rise in India, we might not be able to increase the prices of our services at a proportional rate thereby reducing our margins."
financial_valuation.title: Rising inflation in India and inability to raise prices proportionally

financial_valuation.detail: The Indian economy and its securities markets are influenced by global economic developments and volatility in securities markets in other countries. Negative economic developments in other emerging market countries may affect investor confidence and cause increased volatility in Indian securities markets. Ongoing conflicts are stated to have resulted in and may continue to result in sustained instability across global financial markets.
financial_valuation.evidence: "Developments in the ongoing conflict between Russia and Ukraine, between Israel and Hamas, Hezbollah and Iran and between Houthi forces and certain western countries, have resulted in and may continue to result in a period of sustained instability across global financial markets, induce volatility in commodity prices, times and costs increase in supply chain and logistics, increase borrowing costs, cause outflow of capital from emerging markets".
financial_valuation.title: Global economic conditions and geopolitical conflicts

financial_valuation.detail: Borrowing costs and access to debt capital markets depend significantly on the credit ratings of India. Any adverse revisions by international rating agencies to credit ratings for India and other jurisdictions in which the Company operates may adversely impact the ability to raise additional financing and the interest rates and other commercial terms at which funding is available. A downgrade may occur, for example, upon a change of government tax or fiscal policy, which is outside the Company's control.
financial_valuation.evidence: "This could have an adverse effect on our ability to fund our growth on favourable terms and consequently adversely affect our business, results of operations, cash flows and financial condition and the price of the Equity Shares."
financial_valuation.title: Downgrading of India's sovereign debt rating

financial_valuation.detail: The Restated Financial Information has been compiled from audited financial statements prepared and presented in accordance with Ind-AS and restated in accordance with the SEBI ICDR Regulations. Significant differences exist between Ind-AS, U.S. GAAP and IFRS which may be material to the financial statements contained in the DRHP. Some competitors may not present financial statements in accordance with Ind AS, so their statements may not be directly comparable.
financial_valuation.evidence: "Any reliance by persons not familiar with Ind-AS on the financial disclosures presented in this Draft Red Herring Prospectus should accordingly be limited."
financial_valuation.title: Significant differences between Ind-AS and other accounting principles such as U.S. GAAP and IFRS

financial_valuation.detail: The Offer Price is to be determined on the basis of assessment of market demand through a book-building process and certain quantitative and qualitative factors. Prior to the Offer there has been no public market for the Equity Shares and an active trading market may not develop or be sustained, so any valuation exercise undertaken for the purposes of the Offer would not be based on a benchmark with industry peers. Market capitalisation to revenue and price to earnings multiples are left blank in the DRHP.

The market price could be subject to significant fluctuations after the Offer and may decline below the Offer Price.
financial_valuation.evidence: "We cannot assure you that you will be able to resell their Equity Shares at or above the Offer Price."
financial_valuation.title: Offer Price may not be indicative of the market price after the Offer

The current market price of securities listed pursuant to certain previous initial public offerings managed by the Book Running Lead Managers is below their respective offer prices.

Reference to "Other Regulatory and Statutory Disclosures – Price information of past Offers handled by the BRLMs" on page 366.
financial_valuation.title: Price Band determination and market prices of certain previous BRLM-managed offers below their offer prices

financial_valuation.detail: SEBI and the Stock Exchanges have introduced additional surveillance measures and graded surveillance measures. ASM is based on parameters such as price-to-earnings ratio, percentage of delivery, client concentration, variation in volume of shares and volatility. GSM applies where the quoted price is not commensurate with financial performance and condition measures. Triggering these frameworks could result in restrictions on trading, including higher margin requirements, limiting trading frequency or freezing of price on the upper side of trading.
financial_valuation.evidence: "These restrictions may include requiring higher margin requirements, limiting trading frequency or freezing of price on the upper side of trading, as well as mentioning of our Equity Shares on the surveillance dashboards of the Stock Exchanges."
financial_valuation.title: Possible pre-emptive surveillance measures (ASM and GSM) after listing

financial_valuation.detail: Equity Shares will be quoted in Indian Rupees and dividends will be paid in Indian Rupees and subsequently converted for repatriation. Adverse movement in currency exchange rates during the time taken for conversion may reduce the net dividend to foreign investors, and adverse movement during a delay in repatriating sale proceeds may reduce proceeds received by shareholders.
financial_valuation.evidence: "the exchange rate between the Indian Rupee and the U.S. dollar has fluctuated substantially in recent years and may continue to fluctuate substantially in the future, which may have an adverse effect on the returns on our Equity Shares, independent of our operating results."
financial_valuation.title: Exchange rate fluctuation between the Indian Rupee and foreign currencies

financial_valuation.detail: Prior to the Offer there has been no public market for the Equity Shares and an active trading market may not develop. Listing and quotation do not guarantee that a market will develop or that it will be liquid. Following expiry of the six-month lock-in period on certain portions of the pre-Offer equity share capital, Promoters may sell their shareholding depending on market conditions and investment horizon, and any perception that such sales might occur could affect the trading price.
financial_valuation.evidence: "There has been significant volatility in the Indian stock markets in the recent past, and the trading price of our Equity Shares after this Offer could fluctuate significantly as a result of market volatility or due to various internal or external risks".
financial_valuation.title: Equity Shares have never been publicly traded; potential price and volume fluctuations and absence of an active market

financial_valuation.detail: The Company does not have a formal dividend policy as on the date of the DRHP and has not declared dividends on its Equity Shares during Fiscal 2025, Fiscal 2024 and Fiscal 2023. Ability to pay dividends in the future will depend on dividend policy, future results of operations, financial condition, cash flows, working capital and capital expenditure requirements and other factors, and may also be restricted under certain financing arrangements.
financial_valuation.evidence: "Our Company does not have a formal dividend policy as on the date of this Draft Red Herring Prospectus. Our Company, however, has not declared dividends on our Equity Shares during Fiscal 2025, Fiscal 2024 and Fiscal 2023."
financial_valuation.title: No assurance of payment of dividends in the future

financial_valuation.detail: Under the SEBI ICDR Regulations, QIBs and Non-Institutional Bidders must pay the Bid Amount on submission and are not permitted to withdraw or lower their Bids at any stage after submitting a Bid. Retail Individual Bidders, Eligible Employees bidding in the Employee Reservation Portion and Eligible Shareholders bidding in the Shareholders' Reservation Portion may revise Bids during the Bid/Offer Period and withdraw until the Bid/Offer Closing Date. Events affecting bidders' decisions may arise between the date of Bid submission and Allotment, and Allotment may be completed even if such events occur.
financial_valuation.evidence: Retail Individual Bidders, Eligible Employees and Eligible Shareholders reservation bids are "subject to the Bid Amount being up to ₹ 0.20 million". Listing and commencement of trading required "within six Working Days from the Bid/Offer Closing Date".
financial_valuation.title: QIBs and Non-Institutional Bidders cannot withdraw or lower Bids after submission

financial_valuation.detail: Permission for listing and trading will not be granted until certain actions in relation to the Offer are completed and until Allotment. Equity Shares are required to be listed on BSE and NSE within the time mandated under the UPI Circulars, subject to change in the prescribed timeline, but there is no assurance trading will commence in a timely manner or at all. Any failure or delay in obtaining final listing and trading approvals may restrict the ability to dispose of Equity Shares.
financial_valuation.evidence: "we cannot assure you that the trading in our Equity Shares will commence in a timely manner or at all."
financial_valuation.title: No guarantee of timely listing of the Equity Shares on BSE and NSE

financial_valuation.detail: Under the Companies Act a company having share capital and incorporated in India must offer holders pre-emptive rights to subscribe for a proportionate number of Equity Shares unless waived by special resolution of holders of three-fourths of the Equity Shares who have voted. If the laws of the holder's jurisdiction do not permit exercise of such rights without a filing of an offering document or registration statement, the holder will be unable to exercise them unless the Company makes such a filing, and the Company may elect not to do so, leading to dilution of ownership position.
financial_valuation.evidence: "To the extent that the holders are unable to exercise pre-emptive rights granted in respect of the Equity Shares, they may suffer future dilution of their ownership position and their proportional interests in our Company would be reduced."
financial_valuation.title: Restrictions on the ability of holders to exercise pre-emptive rights under Indian law

financial_valuation.detail: The Company may finance growth through future equity offerings which may dilute investors' shareholdings. Disposal of Equity Shares by shareholders, or the perception that such issuance or sales may occur, including to comply with minimum public shareholding norms, may adversely affect the trading price and lead to difficulty raising capital or incurring additional debt. Disposal, pledge or encumbrance of Equity Shares by Promoters or other shareholders may also affect the trading price, and such securities may be issued at prices below the Offer Price.
financial_valuation.evidence: "Such securities may also be issued at prices below the Offer Price."
financial_valuation.title: Future issuance of Equity Shares or sales by Promoters may dilute holdings and affect the trading price

financial_valuation.detail: If the Company does not receive a minimum subscription of 90% of the Fresh Issue and a subscription as specified under Rule 19(2)(b) of the SCRR, including through devolvement of Underwriters, within sixty days from the Bid/Offer Closing Date, or if the subscription level falls below these thresholds after the Bid/Offer Closing Date on account of withdrawal of applications, technical rejections or any other reason, or if listing or trading permission is not obtained, the Company shall forthwith refund the entire subscription amount. If there is a delay beyond four days, the Company and every Director who is an officer in default shall pay interest as prescribed.
financial_valuation.evidence: "a minimum subscription of 90% of the Fresh Issue"; "within sixty (60) days from the date of Bid/ Offer Closing Date"; "If there is a delay beyond four days, our Company and every Director of our Company who is an officer in default, to the extent applicable, shall pay interest as prescribed under applicable law."
financial_valuation.title: Offer may fail if minimum subscription of 90% of the Fresh Issue is not received

internal_operational.detail: The Company has one manufacturing facility at Palghar, Maharashtra, about 100 km from Mumbai along NH-8. Operations involve manufacturing, storage and transportation subject to operating risks including malfunction or failure of equipment, industrial accidents, severe weather and natural disasters. Any breakdown of machinery, laboratories, automation systems or IT systems (together "Manufacturing Assets") may entail significant repair costs and cause delays, suspension or full or partial shutdown, and planned shutdowns may be required for maintenance, statutory inspections, customer audits and capacity expansion.
internal_operational.evidence: "We have manufacturing facility in Palghar, Maharashtra, about 100 km from Mumbai along National Highway 8 (NH-8)"; "Although we have not had any incidents during six months period ended September 30, 2025 and Fiscal 2025, Fiscal 2024 or Fiscal 2023, we cannot assure you that we will not experience any malfunction or failure of our Manufacturing Assets in the future."
internal_operational.title: Dependence on the single Palghar manufacturing facility and manufacturing-process risks

internal_operational.detail: Business is heavily concentrated on supplying generic formulation products to Government Customers under procurement contracts won through tenders, for Central Government projects under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare through GoI agencies and state government agencies. New projects are awarded through competitive bidding and pre-qualification criteria; projects are mostly one-time and not subject to automatic renewal. Adverse change in budgetary allocations, policy changes, insufficiency of funds or changed qualification criteria could reduce contracts available for bidding or delay awards. Bank guarantees may be required as part of project contracts and the ability to recover compensation on termination by government authorities is limited.
internal_operational.evidence: Total Government Customers revenue: ₹1,012.93 million / 89.93% (six months ended September 30, 2025); ₹1,996.04 million / 90.83% (Fiscal 2025); ₹1,829.02 million / 98.14% (Fiscal 2024); ₹1,719.81 million / 99.79% (Fiscal 2023). Split for six months ended September 30, 2025: Central agencies ₹204.05 million / 18.12%, State agencies ₹808.88 million / 71.82%. Private customers ₹113.39 million / 10.07% (six months ended September 30, 2025) versus ₹3.58 million / 0.21% (Fiscal 2023). Bid win ratio: 78.57% (28 bids, 6 lost, 22 won) for six months ended September 30, 2025 with 20 bids awaiting results; 63.95% (86 bids, 31 lost, 55 won) Fiscal 2025; 59.60% (99 bids, 40 lost, 59 won) Fiscal 2024; 69.70% (66 bids, 20 lost, 46 won) Fiscal 2023.
internal_operational.title: Revenue concentration on Government Customers won through competitive tenders

Some customers may start manufacturing at their own facilities and discontinue use of the Company's services and products. Capital expenditure is incurred for future periods, and delays in contracting for utilisation of upcoming capacity may result in no proportionate increase in revenue relative to an installed capacity increase. Certain customer names are not disclosed in the DRHP due to non-receipt of consent.

internal_operational.title: Dependence on a limited number of customers

internal_operational.detail: Products and manufacturing processes are subject to quality standards and specifications set by customers. Deviations may lead to product recall, cancellation of orders, indemnity and warranty claims, monetary liability and litigation. Customers are typically entitled to audit the Company's manufacturing facilities, processes or systems. Agreements typically require the Company to bear the expenses and costs of returns, either upfront or by deduction from bills; stated reasons for returns include incorrect consignee, damaged products, late delivery and short shelf life.
internal_operational.evidence: Product returns of ₹35.24 million, ₹36.66 million, ₹17.58 million and ₹17.73 million, amounting to 3.13%, 1.67%, 0.94% and 1.03% of revenue from operations for the six months ended September 30, 2025, Fiscal 2025, Fiscal 2024 and Fiscal 2023 respectively. "While we have not received any adverse observations in the six months period ended September 30, 2025 and Fiscal Year ended 2025, 2024 and 2023 ... from our customers pursuant to such audits".
internal_operational.title: Failure to comply with customer quality requirements and technical specifications; product returns and warranty claims

Sale and purchase agreements were executed on December 13, 2025, but completion will occur after the date of the DRHP. There is no assurance completion will occur as contemplated, including due to delays in obtaining regulatory, contractual or third-party approvals or fulfilling conditions precedent, which may result in the Company continuing to operate from leased premises for an extended period.

internal_operational.title: Completion risk on the agreement to purchase the Palghar Unit 1 and Unit 2 land and premises from Promoters

internal_operational.detail: Recent amendments to the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945 make marketing companies, in addition to the actual manufacturer, responsible for the quality of the drug and for regulatory compliance. Products are subject to contamination, adulteration and product tampering during production, transportation or storage. Claims may also arise from manufacturing defects, negligence in storage or handling, or deterioration in quality controls. A partially successful or completely uninsured claim could materially harm the business.
internal_operational.evidence: "A partially successful or completely uninsured claim against us could materially harm our business, results of operations and financial condition."; "Product liability claims, regardless of their merits or the ultimate success of the defense against them, are expensive."
internal_operational.title: Rejection of supplied products and product liability claims arising from product defects

internal_operational.detail: APIs, excipients, impurities and primary and secondary packaging materials are purchased from third-party suppliers domestically. The Company has no long-term contracts with third-party suppliers; prices are negotiated for each purchase order. Suppliers may be unable to supply sufficient quantities at acceptable prices, and one or more existing suppliers may discontinue operations.

Purchase of stock in trade ₹110.43 million / 12.12%, ₹194.45 million / 11.29%, ₹33.43 million / 2.25%, nil. Largest supplier ₹110.43 million / 19.33% of cost of materials (six months ended September 30, 2025), ₹68.82 million / 6.26% (Fiscal 2025), ₹38.67 million / 4.76% (Fiscal 2024), ₹60.18 million / 7.09% (Fiscal 2023). internal_operational.title: Shortfall in raw material supply, raw material price increases and supplier concentration

internal_operational.detail: Channel partners facilitate distribution, coordinate dispatches, provide local support, ensure timely delivery, obtain acknowledgements from customers or institutions and assist in collection of payments. The Company does not have exclusive arrangements with channel partners, which allows them to engage with competitors. Risks listed include failure to renew agreements, inability to identify replacement partners, failure to obtain timely payments, reduction or cancellation of orders and disruption in delivery.
internal_operational.evidence: "Further, we do not have exclusive arrangements with our channel partners, which allows them to engage with our competitors."
internal_operational.title: Reliance on non-exclusive channel partners for delivery and local support

internal_operational.detail: The Company depends on senior management, Promoters and Executive Directors, and on its ability to attract and retain personnel with technical expertise. Competition for qualified technical, product development and sales personnel is described as intense. The Company does not have key man insurance policies as of the date of the DRHP.

internal_operational.title: Dependence on management team and key managerial personnel; high employee attrition and absence of key man insurance

internal_operational.detail: All manufacturing facilities are located in Palghar, Maharashtra, concentrating the entire current manufacturing operation in one geographic area. This heightens exposure to regulatory, economic, demographic and other changes in Palghar, natural and man-made disasters, labour unrest, terrorist attacks and other acts of violence, and to state government policies on taxes, duties and incentives.
internal_operational.evidence: "As of the date of this Draft Red Herring Prospectus, all of our manufacturing facilities are located in Palghar, Maharashtra."; "while Palghar has not experienced social and civil unrest in the the six months period ended September 30, 2025 and Fiscal Year ended 2025, 2024 and 2023, within the state, there can be no assurance that such situations will not occur in the future."
internal_operational.title: Geographic concentration of all manufacturing facilities in Palghar, Maharashtra

internal_operational.detail: Operations depend on availability of labour and good relationships with the labour force. Employees are not members of any organised labour union as of the date of the DRHP. Work stoppages such as strikes and lockouts may adversely affect operations. The Company engages contract labour through independent contractors and remains responsible for wage payments to such labourers in the event of default by the contractors.
internal_operational.evidence: "As on September 30, 2025, we had 616 employees working in our manufacturing facilities."; "Although we have not had instances of strikes and major labour disputes, we may experience strikes or lockouts on account of labour disputes in the future."
internal_operational.title: Potential labour disruptions and liability for contract labour wages

internal_operational.detail: Future success may depend in part on responding to technological advancements and emerging standards in the pharmaceutical business on a cost-effective and timely basis. Rapid and frequent changes in technology and market demand can render existing technologies and equipment obsolete, requiring substantial new capital expenditure or write-down of assets, and implementation of new or upgraded technology may not be cost effective.
internal_operational.evidence: "rapid and frequent changes in technology and market demand can often render existing technologies and equipment obsolete, requiring substantial new capital expenditures or write-down of assets."
internal_operational.title: Cost of implementing new technologies

internal_operational.detail: Products manufactured by the Company or for its customers may cause side effects from factors outside the Company's control, or may be perceived to cause side effects when misused or when the cause of side effects is not conclusively determined, including where other companies' products containing the same or similar APIs, raw materials or delivery technologies cause or are perceived to cause side effects. Listed consequences include injury or death of patients, a fall in demand and sales, recall or withdrawal of products, withdrawal or cancellation of regulatory approvals for the product or the production facility, brand and reputational damage, and lawsuits and regulatory investigations resulting in liabilities, fines or sanctions.
internal_operational.evidence: "withdrawal or cancellation of regulatory approvals for the relevant products or the relevant production facility"; "exposure to lawsuits and regulatory investigation relating to the relevant products that result in liabilities, fines or sanctions."
internal_operational.title: Products causing or being perceived to cause side effects

internal_operational.detail: The Company tracks operational metrics, including non-GAAP metrics, with internal systems and tools that may differ from estimates or similar metrics published by third parties due to differences in sources, methodologies or assumptions. These metrics are not a measurement of financial performance or liquidity under Ind AS, are not standardised terms, and may not be directly comparable with similarly titled metrics of other companies. Internal systems may undercount or over count performance or contain algorithmic or other technical errors.
internal_operational.evidence: Metrics named: "Net PAT margin, Return on net worth (RoNW), Return on capital employed (RoCE), Debt/Equity, EBITDA, EBITDA Margin"; "investors should not place undue reliance on the non-GAAP financial information included in this Draft Red Herring Prospectus."
internal_operational.title: Operational and non-GAAP metrics tracked with internal systems are subject to measurement limitations

internal_operational.detail: The Company maintains policies covering material damage to buildings, plant and machinery, furniture, fixtures, fittings and stocks, a marine sales turnover policy covering transit by sea, air, rail, road and courier, and a directors and officers liability policy, but has not procured insurance against all risks and liabilities and has no key man insurance. Insured assets have been below total assets in each period presented.
internal_operational.evidence: Total assets including net block of PPE, CWIP, investment property, ROU assets and inventory: ₹830.38 million / ₹694.35 million / ₹414.67 million / ₹317.70 million. Sum insured of assets: ₹693.47 million / ₹323.37 million / ₹256.26 million / ₹139.42 million. Percentage of insurance coverage: 83.54% (six months ended September 30, 2025), 46.57% (March 31, 2025), 61.80% (March 31, 2024), 43.88% (March 31, 2023). Certified by Statutory Auditor JAIN V & CO, FRN 116303W, certificate dated January 02, 2026.
internal_operational.title: Insurance coverage may not adequately protect against all losses

internal_operational.detail: IT, ERP and quality control solutions cover operations, product development, quality control, procurement, dispatch and accounting, and automation systems and software automate manufacturing and production. These systems are vulnerable to damage or interruption from cyber-attacks, infrastructure failures, compromises to physical security and damaging weather. Malfunction of data system security measures could enable unauthorized persons to access sensitive business data, including intellectual property or business strategy information of the Company or its customers.
internal_operational.evidence: "A significant or large-scale malfunction or interruption of one or more of our IT, ERP or quality control systems or manufacturing automation systems could adversely affect our ability to keep our operations running efficiently and affect product availability".
internal_operational.title: Failure or disruption of IT, manufacturing automation and ERP systems

internal_operational.detail: Under certain customer arrangements the Company pays freight costs for products sold and may pay transportation costs for delivery of raw materials and inputs. It relies on third-party transportation and logistics providers with whom it has no long-term contractual arrangements, and those providers do not carry insurance coverage, so losses arising during transportation must be claimed under the Company's own insurance policy.
internal_operational.evidence: Freight charges ₹22.17 million / 2.43% of total expenses (six months ended September 30, 2025), ₹50.40 million / 2.93% (Fiscal 2025), ₹41.18 million / 2.78% (Fiscal 2024), ₹37.14 million / 2.48% (Fiscal 2023). "our third party transportation providers do not carry any insurance coverage".
internal_operational.title: Dependence on third-party transportation and logistics providers without long-term contracts or insurance

internal_operational.detail: The business depends on an adequate and uninterrupted supply of electricity, water and natural gas at reasonable cost, procured from third parties. Reliance on third parties exposes the Company to shortage or breakdown in supply, the correction of which is in the hands of such third parties, and there is no assurance alternate sources can be secured in a timely manner at commercially reasonable cost.
internal_operational.evidence: "Any interruption in the continuous supply of water, gas, and electricity may negatively impact our manufacturing processes, which may result in delays in delivery of our products or non-delivery, resulting in loss of revenue and damage to our reputation or customer relationships."
internal_operational.title: Dependence on third parties for utilities at manufacturing facilities

internal_operational.detail: Entities in India and international locations could pass off their own products as the Company's generic products, including counterfeit or pirated products imitating brand names or packaging materials, or attempting to create look-alike generic drug products. Counterfeit products are described as unsafe or ineffective and potentially life-threatening.
internal_operational.evidence: "Although no such incidents have happened in the the six months period ended September 30, 2025 and Fiscal Year ended 2025, 2024 and 2023, any such counterfeits or pirated products could reduce our market share due to replacement of demand for our products and adversely affect our goodwill."
internal_operational.title: Counterfeit generic products passed off as the Company's products

internal_operational.detail: Customer agreements contain confidentiality and non-disclosure clauses requiring the Company to keep know-how and technical specifications confidential. Most of these contracts do not contain provisions limiting the Company's liability with respect to breaches of the confidentiality obligation. Breach or alleged breach may lead customers to terminate engagements or initiate litigation for breach of contract and to seek damages and compensation.
internal_operational.evidence: "most of these contracts do not contain provisions limiting our liability with respect to breaches of our obligation to keep the information we receive from them confidential"; "we have not had any incidents of breach of our confidentiality agreements in the six months period ended September 30, 2025 and Fiscal Year ended 2025, 2024 and 2023".
internal_operational.title: Failure to maintain confidentiality of customer information

internal_operational.detail: Installed capacity and capacity utilisation information for the Palghar facilities is based on assumptions and estimates of management taken into account by an independent chartered engineer. Installed capacity is calculated using the equipment manufacturer's rated maximum capacity adjusted for typical achieved capacity across processes and batch sizes in a sequential line setup, with allowance for downtime from product changeover cleaning, scheduled breaks and material loading and unloading. Industry players use different methodologies.
internal_operational.evidence: "The assumptions and estimates taken into account include that our manufacturing facility operates for 356 days in a year in two daily shifts for installed capacity as notional capacity for capacity utilization." Independent chartered engineer: Sharjeel Aslam Faiz. Note in the capacity table states installed capacity is calculated on 356 days working with 10 hours operations shift for a multi-product facility.
internal_operational.title: Installed capacity information is based on management assumptions and estimates

internal_operational.detail: India has experienced natural calamities such as earthquakes and floods, as well as the global Covid-19 pandemic. Such events could damage or destroy manufacturing facilities or other assets, disrupt equipment, machines, information systems, electrical systems and telecommunication services for sustained periods and make it difficult for employees to reach business locations. India has also from time to time experienced social, religious and civil unrest and hostilities between neighbouring countries; military activity or terrorist attacks could disrupt communications and make travel and logistics more difficult.
internal_operational.evidence: "Though some of the losses are covered under appropriate insurance, the above factors may still adversely affect our business, results of operations, cash flows and financial condition."
internal_operational.title: Natural calamities, climate change, epidemics and pandemics, hostilities, terrorist attacks and civil unrest in India

internal_operational.detail: India's physical infrastructure is less developed than that of many developed nations. Congestion or disruption in the electricity grid, road and rail networks, communication systems or other public facilities could disrupt normal business activity or supply channels, and deterioration of physical infrastructure would disrupt the pharmaceutical industry and add costs to doing business in India.
internal_operational.evidence: "Any deterioration of India's physical infrastructure would harm the national economy, disrupt the pharmaceutical industry, which are important to our business, and add costs to doing business in India."
internal_operational.title: Extent and reliability of Indian infrastructure

strategy_growth.detail: The Company competes in the domestic generics business on therapeutic product categories and, within each category, on dosage strengths and drug delivery. The Indian pharmaceutical industry is highly fragmented. Competition is on the basis of product portfolio, supply (quality, regulatory compliance and financial stability), service (on-time delivery and manufacturing flexibility) and cost-effective manufacturing, and may result in a decrease in prices paid. Some competitors may have substantially greater financial, marketing, technical or other resources. As the international business commences, competition is expected from major international generic manufacturers.
strategy_growth.evidence: "The Indian pharmaceutical industry is highly fragmented, with over 10,000 manufacturers in both the organised and unorganised sectors. Pharmaceutical manufacturing is primarily concentrated in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Uttarakhand, and Himachal Pradesh. As per the Confederation of Indian Industries (CII), approximately 8,000 small and medium enterprises (SMEs) make up about 70% of the total pharmaceutical units in India. (Source: CareEdge Report)"
strategy_growth.title: Highly competitive market for generic products in India

strategy_growth.detail: Substantially all revenues are generated by sales of generic products, and future profitability depends to a significant extent on continued portfolio expansion through product development activities. The formulation and adaptation of post-patent products is described as complex, time-consuming and costly, characterised by significant upfront costs including product development, obtaining regulatory approvals, building inventory and sales and marketing. New products may not perform as expected, may be less profitable than historically experienced or estimated, may be loss-making, may consume substantial financial resources or divert management attention.
strategy_growth.evidence: "Our portfolio grew from 661 products as of March 31, 2023 to 871 products as of March 31, 2025 ... As of September 30, 2025, our product portfolio comprised 948 products." New products introduced: 77 (six months ended September 30, 2025, portfolio 948), 122 (Fiscal 2025, portfolio 871), 88 (Fiscal 2024, portfolio 749), 17 (Fiscal 2023, portfolio 661). Product development team of 10 employees as of September 30, 2025.
strategy_growth.title: Dependence on product development activities and continued generic portfolio expansion

strategy_growth.detail: The Company plans to expand its generic formulations business-to-government business internationally to supply foreign government customers in semi-regulated and unregulated countries, excluding the United States, European Union and Japan, by participating in government tenders and obtaining product approvals and import licenses. Disclosed risks include regulatory ambiguity with minimal documentation requirements and sudden enforcement of local standards, unpredictable tender processes with opaque evaluation criteria, delayed payment from government agencies, risk of counterfeit substitution, compliance burden requiring international certifications, political and policy instability, limited market visibility and demand data, local partner and distribution risks and reputational exposure, in addition to customary international risks such as foreign currency volatility, changes in foreign laws and trade restrictions, tariffs, quotas, anti-dumping or countervailing measures and economic instability or political unrest.
strategy_growth.evidence: "Payment cycles under government schemes in these semi-regulated or unregulated countries can stretch from several months to even a year."; "We, as exporter of products into the semi-regulated or unregulated countries, are required to maintain international certifications such as WHO-GMP and ISO in order to be eligible to participate in government schemes." (Source: CareEdge Report)
strategy_growth.title: Planned international expansion of the generic formulations B2G business into semi-regulated and unregulated countries

strategy_growth.detail: The Company plans to begin manufacture and supply of cosmetic products and to participate in procurement tenders of GoI and state government agencies for air freshener, body spray, deodorizing talc, face wash, fragrance body spray, hair shampoo, hand wash, moisturizing lotion and sunscreen lotion. These will be manufactured at the new Unit at the Palghar facility, whose premises have been constructed while plant and equipment procurement is in process and the Unit is under commissioning. There is no assurance new cosmetic products will achieve success, win tenders, or gain market acceptance, and hiring, training and retaining qualified employees in this segment may be more difficult than for competitors.
strategy_growth.evidence: "We received our license from the Food & Drugs Administration (Maharashtra State) on May 27, 2025 which is valid until May 26, 2030." "India's skincare market rose from US$2.87 billion in CY 2020 to US$3.67 billion in CY 2024 and is set to reach US$ 5.32 billion by CY 2028, showing a 10% CAGR. (Source: CareEdge Report)"
strategy_growth.title: Entry into cosmetic products manufacture and supply, a new business for the Company

strategy_growth.detail: The Company acquired plots at Saykha Industrial Estate, Bharuch, Gujarat from GIDC to establish an API manufacturing facility and obtained statutory approvals including environmental clearance from SEIAA Gujarat and approval for disposal of hazardous and incinerable wastes from BEIL Infrastructure Limited. Construction has not commenced; management has deferred commencement having regard to prevailing market conditions, connectivity-related constraints, uncertainties in the API sector and the significant capital outlay required, determining that near-term execution may not be commercially viable. As the plots were not utilised within the GIDC-prescribed timeframe, the Company has applied for an extension. Continued deferral may lead to technological obsolescence, higher compliance and holding costs and uncertainty regarding recovery of the land investment.
strategy_growth.evidence: "Our Company acquired Plot Nos. DP/87 and DP/88, admeasuring 30,008.160 sq. meters, at Saykha Industrial Estate, Bharuch, Gujarat, from the Gujarat Industrial Development Corporation (GIDC) pursuant to an agreement dated September 24, 2021, with possession obtained on September 30, 2021." "our Company has applied to GIDC for an extension for utilization of the allotted plots up to March 31, 2027. There can be no assurance that such extension will be granted by GIDC, and, even if granted, if we are unable to utilize the allotted plots within the extended timeline, GIDC may take actions against us, including, without limitation, levying non-utilization penalties and/or evicting us from the allotted plots." API Manufacturing plot leased for 99 years at ₹76,250,734 lumpsum; "The API manufacturing unit is not in operation."
strategy_growth.title: Indefinite deferral of the proposed API manufacturing facility at Bharuch, Gujarat

strategy_growth.detail: The Company intends to implement several business strategies aimed at business growth and improvement of market position, each subject to risks and uncertainties. Strategies may not succeed due to factors including inability to reduce operating costs, failure to develop new products and services with growth potential as market preferences change, failure to execute agreements with technology and strategic partners, failure to effectively market new products and services, failure to sufficiently upgrade infrastructure, machines, automation, equipment and technology, failure to maintain quality and consistency or to scale operations, changes in GoI policy or regulation and inability to respond to competition.
strategy_growth.evidence: "Any failure on our part to implement our strategy due to many reasons as attributed aforesaid could be detrimental to our long-term business outlook and our growth prospects".
strategy_growth.title: Inability to implement business strategies in a timely manner or at all

strategy_growth.detail: The Company has made and intends to continue making investments to expand manufacturing capacity, adding Unit 2 at the Palghar facility. The new Unit has been constructed and application has been made for the required licenses; Unit 2 is under commissioning and production is yet to commence. Expansion requires governmental, statutory and other regulatory approvals, licenses, permits and registrations, and failure to obtain or renew them in a timely manner may delay the commissioning date.
strategy_growth.evidence: "As of September 30, 2025, project cost of ₹358.07 million have been incurred."
strategy_growth.title: Capacity expansion plans subject to delays in implementation and cost overruns

strategy_growth.detail: Pharmaceutical companies have been undertaking efforts including pursuing new patents for existing products granted just before the expiration of earlier patents, which could extend patent protection or delay the launch of generics; selling the brand product as an authorized generic directly, through an affiliate or by a marketing partner; and enacting legislation restricting the substitution of some generic drugs. If such efforts are successful, introductions of the Company's generic products may be delayed.
strategy_growth.evidence: "If pharmaceutical companies or other third parties are successful in limiting the use of generic products through these or other means, introductions of our generic products may be delayed, and our business, results of operations, and financial condition may be adversely affected."
strategy_growth.title: Delay in launching new generic products due to third-party efforts to limit generic use

concerns_observed: Cash generation moved the opposite way to profit for three straight years: CFO Rs 332.85 million (Fiscal 2023) to Rs 198.91 million (Fiscal 2024) to Rs 107.67 million (Fiscal 2025) while PAT went Rs 222.50 million to Rs 341.38 million to Rs 412.66 million, so Fiscal 2025 CFO was roughly a quarter of that year's PAT; CFO in the six months ended September 30, 2025 was Rs 68.04 million.

Receivables are absorbing the business: trade receivables Rs 450.91 million, Rs 493.43 million, Rs 673.20 million and Rs 857.18 million across Fiscals 2023, 2024, 2025 and September 30, 2025 - 76.10% of the six-month revenue from operations against 30.64%, 26.48% and 26.16% in the three Fiscals - with debtor days 97 / 92 / 97 / 124 against a stated customer realisation cycle of 60-120 days.

Capacity is heavily under-used before a second unit is added: Unit 1 utilisation in the six months ended September 30, 2025 was 22.22% on tablets (installed 9,500 million), 1.16% on capsules (1,500 million), 5.72% on sachets, 10.60% on syrups, 6.80% on external liquid, 0.40% on aerosol and 0.60% on external powder, with no production at all on combi blister packs (30 million packets), kits (0.6 million packets) or surgical dressing (5.00 million sachets); tablets ran at 53.24% in Fiscal 2025 and 40.55% in Fiscal 2024.

Unit 2 is built but cannot yet produce: Rs 358.07 million of project cost was incurred as of September 30, 2025, the DRHP states applications have been made for the required licences and that Unit 2 is under commissioning with production yet to commence, and its expected installed capacity of 2,500 million tablets, 30 million external liquid, 50 million ointments and 17.50 million creams would be added on top of the utilisation levels above.

The revenue base is one buyer type won one contract at a time: Government Customers were 99.79%, 98.14%, 90.83% and 89.93% of revenue from operations; the DRHP states projects are awarded through competitive bidding, are mostly one-time and are not subject to automatic renewal; the largest customer alone was Rs 235.35 million / 20.90% in the six months ended September 30, 2025 against 13.38% in Fiscal 2025, and the top 10 were 65.43% against 61.08%.

Almost every operating asset the business runs on belongs to the promoter family: Unit 1 is leased from Rajesh Vasantray Doshi and Bhavna Rajesh Doshi at Rs 1,818,500 per month and Unit 2 from Rajesh Vasantray Doshi, Krishiv Rajesh Doshi and Bhavna Rajesh Doshi at Rs 852,600 per month; the Registered Office, Corporate Office units and other offices are leased from Promoter and Promoter Group; and the corporate logo plus sixteen registered trademarks are licensed from Rajesh Vasantray Doshi under a deed dated April 01, 2025 against royalty.

Title to the manufacturing site has not passed: sale and purchase agreements for the Palghar Unit 1 and Unit 2 land and premises were executed with the Promoters on December 13, 2025, but the DRHP states completion will occur after the date of the Draft Red Herring Prospectus and that legal title to the underlying land parcels has not yet been transferred to the Company.

Employee turnover is high and worst where it matters most: attrition was 18.40% (Fiscal 2023), 25.00% (Fiscal 2024), 38.33% (Fiscal 2025) and 17.20% in the six months ended September 30, 2025 on average headcount of 282 / 277 / 264 / 268, while product development attrition was 35.29%, 40.00%, 40.00% and 40.00% against a product development team of only 10 employees at September 30, 2025 - and there is no key man insurance.

The senior layer turned over within months of the filing: Additional Executive Director Dayanad S Mathapati ceased on July 01, 2025 having been appointed on April 27, 2025, Executive Director Vijay Manharlal Gadhia ceased on July 10, 2025, and the restated related-party note carries two Chief Financial Officers (Subhash Ruia and Amit Bakul Panchal) and two Company Secretaries (Darshita Shah and Nidhi Bagadia) across the periods presented.

Board experience for a listed environment is absent by the issuer's own statement: all Promoters, who are also Directors, do not have prior experience serving as promoters or directors of any listed entity; the Board is six with three Independent Directors, and Executive Director Krishiv Rajesh Doshi, aged 23 and son of the Chairman and Managing Director, was appointed on August 11, 2025 with over four years of experience in the healthcare industry.

Input concentration jumped sharply in the latest period: the largest supplier was 4.76% of cost of materials in Fiscal 2024 and 6.26% in Fiscal 2025 but Rs 110.43 million / 19.33% in the six months ended September 30, 2025, top 10 suppliers went 35.57% / 36.17% / 50.48%, and the Company states it has no long-term contracts with third-party suppliers; cost of materials consumed was 57.03%, 51.83%, 51.79% and 48.15% of total expenses.

Product returns are rising, not falling: Rs 17.73 million / 1.03% of revenue from operations (Fiscal 2023), Rs 17.58 million / 0.94% (Fiscal 2024), Rs 36.66 million / 1.67% (Fiscal 2025) and Rs 35.24 million / 3.13% in the six months ended September 30, 2025, with stated causes including damaged products, late delivery and short shelf life and the cost borne by the Company.

Therapeutic and geographic mix swings hard with tender outcomes rather than with demand: Antiparasitic went 13.06% (Fiscal 2023) to 6.31% to 8.38% to 0.08% of revenue in the six months ended September 30, 2025; Maharashtra went 16.85% / 26.16% / 18.87% to 46.22%; Tamil Nadu 23.31% to 14.23% and Karnataka 16.10% to 12.23% over the same step.

Off-balance-sheet exposure is concentrated in tender guarantees: contingent liabilities and commitments were Rs 340.49 million at September 30, 2025 (17.28% of net worth) against Rs 305.75 million, Rs 202.98 million and Rs 173.75 million, of which bank guarantees against tenders were Rs 328.37 million; Rs 282.33 million of the Rs 500.00 million sanctioned non-fund-based limit was utilised as on November 30, 2025.

The DRHP prints two conflicting EBITDA series: the Other Financial Information table fails its own stated formula in three of the four periods presented, and the figures used here are from the KPI-comparison table that reproduces from the restated P&L. The DRHP separately warns that its non-GAAP metrics - Net PAT margin, RoNW, RoCE, Debt/Equity, EBITDA and EBITDA Margin - are tracked with internal systems that may undercount or over count performance.

CARO observations run across all three Fiscals: undisputed income tax of Rs 1.04 million for AY 2023-24 in arrears more than six months at March 31, 2025; the resignation of previous statutory auditor M/s TMG and Associates during Fiscal 2024; and CSR amounts earmarked but unspent of Rs 4.08 million (Fiscal 2024) and Rs 4.40 million (Fiscal 2023), alongside a disclosed delay in transferring unspent CSR within the stipulated 30 days for financial year 2022-23.
data_gaps: This is a DRHP-stage filing: Price Band, Offer Price, Offer size in value terms, gross and net proceeds, post-Offer capital, the post-Offer promoter percentage and the market-capitalisation-to-revenue and price-to-earnings cells all print as placeholders, so no valuation, no market capitalisation and no comparison against the disclosed industry P/E range of 25.70 to 35.25 can be made from this document.

Capacity disclosure could not be routed to the business bundle: the pipeline found 34 topic marks in the document (21 in risk factors, 9 in business) but none reached the business_ops extract, and the Manufacturing - Capacity, Production and Utilization table on page 211 is image-locked. The utilisation percentages used here come from risk-factor evidence rather than from that table, and no unit-wise production volumes or a combined installed-capacity total could be established.

The auditor-certified weighted average cost of acquisition per Equity Share could not be routed: the certificate dated January 3, 2026 issued by JAIN V & CO is referenced only as a material document, evidence marks were found in the extraction (9 in basis, 6 in summary) but the table itself does not appear in the routed text, so the promoter's average acquisition cost is unestablished rather than undisclosed.

No cash conversion cycle is stated and none was constructed. The DRHP prints a Net Working Capital Days metric that is not built as debtor plus inventory less creditor days, so it was deliberately not labelled a cash conversion cycle; debtor, inventory and creditor days are recorded separately at 124 / 28 / 26 for the six months to September 30, 2025 and 97 / 18 / 20 for Fiscal 2025.

Total employee strength is not disclosed in the routed sections, and the available figures do not reconcile: 616 employees working in the manufacturing facilities as on September 30, 2025 in the risk factors, against an average number of employees of 268 for the same period (264, 277 and 282 in Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023) in the attrition disclosure.

Two conflicting EBITDA series exist in the document. The Other Financial Information table fails its own stated formula in three of the four periods presented; the figures used here come from the KPI-comparison table, which reproduces from the restated P&L. The DRHP's own risk factor warns its non-GAAP metrics may undercount or over count performance.

The Fiscal 2025 cash flow table does not foot: CFO plus CFI plus CFF as printed sums to Rs -78.61 million against a stated net decrease in cash of Rs -78.63 million. The Rs 0.02 million difference is a rounding gap in the DRHP's own table, not an extraction error.

Return on equity is not disclosed for any period, and the RoCE of 12.86% and RoNW of 9.71% shown for the six months ended September 30, 2025 are printed without any statement that they are annualised, so they are not directly comparable with the full-year RoCE of 33.13%, 37.25% and 31.76%.

Financial information for the sole Group Company, Hindustan Capital Private Limited - reserves excluding revaluation reserve, sales, profit after tax, earnings per share, diluted earnings per share and net asset value for Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023 - is hosted on the Company's website and expressly does not form part of the DRHP, so the counterparty on the Rs 816.8 lakhs of loans taken and repaid in Fiscal 2025 cannot be assessed from the document.

The Government and Other Approvals chapter states it discloses Material Approvals (a) applied for but not received, (b) which have expired with renewal to be applied for, and (c) required but not obtained or applied for, but the supplied extract ends before those items are enumerated, so no individual approval from that list could be recorded. Separately, the DRHP states certain of the 948 product registrations may have lapsed in their normal course without identifying which or how many.

The Minimum Promoters' Contribution lock-in table is entirely placeholder text to be updated at the Prospectus stage - no lock-in expiry date, share count or acquisition price is disclosed - and the anchor lock-ins are given only as 30-day and 90-day periods with no dates.

The listed-peer table carries no stated unit for the total income column (Ajanta Pharma 7,778.96, Syncom Formulations (India) 4,824.47, Windlas Biotech 47,426.00), so peer scale cannot be set against the Company's revenue from operations of Rs 2,197.46 million; the DRHP itself states there are no directly comparable peers fully aligned with its product profile and B2G model, and discloses no market share.

No contracted or unexecuted order value is disclosed for any tender, and customer names are withheld for want of consent, so the customer representing 20.90% of revenue in the six months to September 30, 2025 cannot be identified or traced across periods.

Interest rates are not disclosed at facility level: working capital facilities are given only as EBLR plus 0.20%, the Rs 385.0 lakhs related-party loan carries a stated Nil rate, and no rate is printed against the bank guarantee, cash credit or letter of credit sub-limits.

Litigation amounts are not additive to a single total and no combined figure is printed: Rs 106.9 lakhs across 3 proceedings against the Company and Rs 200.0 lakhs across 7 proceedings against the Promoters, with nil against Directors, Key Managerial Personnel and Senior Management, against a Materiality Threshold of Rs 16.20 million.
monitorables: CFO against PAT in Fiscal 2026 and Fiscal 2027 - whether the Rs 107.67 million against Rs 412.66 million gap of Fiscal 2025 narrows, and whether debtor days retrace from 124 toward the 92-97 range of Fiscals 2023-2025.

Receipt of the outstanding licences for Palghar Unit 2 and the date production actually commences, against the Rs 358.07 million already incurred and Rs 370.43 million held in capital work-in-progress.

Unit 1 utilisation, particularly tablets (22.22% in the six months to September 30, 2025 against 53.24% in Fiscal 2025) and capsules (1.16%), and whether combi blister packs, kits and surgical dressing move off nil production.

Deployment of the Rs 725.00 million working capital object across Fiscal 2027 against the monitoring agency's quarterly reports under Regulation 41, and the amount finally allocated to general corporate purposes within the 25% of Gross Proceeds cap.

Outcome of the three Drugs and Cosmetics Act prosecutions, in particular Dindigul matter STC/0000213/2024 currently stayed by the Madras High Court, and any consequential effect on tender eligibility or on the 948 product registrations.

Any order or communication from the Registrar of Companies on adjudication application SRN AC0216592 filed December 21, 2025, and whether the Fiscal 2026 CARO annexure carries fresh observations after the Fiscal 2023-2025 sequence on statutory dues, auditor resignation and unspent CSR.
Completion of the December 13, 2025 sale and purchase agreements transferring title of the Palghar Unit 1 and Unit 2 land and premises from the Promoters to the Company.

Bid win ratio and pipeline conversion - 22 of 28 won with 20 awaiting results at September 30, 2025 against 55 of 86 in Fiscal 2025 - and whether Government Customers stay near 90% or the private channel builds on 10.07%.

Customer top-1 share, which moved from 13.38% in Fiscal 2025 to 20.90% in the six months to September 30, 2025, and supplier top-1 share, which moved from 6.26% to 19.33% of cost of materials over the same step.

Tender bank guarantees outstanding against the Rs 500.00 million sanctioned non-fund-based limit (Rs 328.37 million at September 30, 2025; Rs 282.33 million utilised at November 30, 2025) and contingent liabilities against net worth (17.28% at September 30, 2025).

Whether the promoter's Rs 385.0 lakhs interest-free loan repayable on demand, the Rs 674.9 lakhs security deposit receivable and the monthly lease and royalty streams are re-approved by the Audit Committee and shareholders once listed-company related-party governance applies.

Employee and product-development attrition against 38.33% and 40.00% in Fiscal 2025, and stability of the Chief Financial Officer and Company Secretary positions after the changes recorded across the restated periods.
Whether GIDC grants the extension to March 31, 2027 for plots DP/87 and DP/88 at Saykha, and whether any non-utilisation penalty or eviction action follows.

open_questions: Why did CFO fall to Rs 107.67 million in Fiscal 2025 on PAT of Rs 412.66 million, and how much of the Rs 857.18 million receivable balance at September 30, 2025 is past the stated 60-120 day realisation cycle - the DRHP records nil trade receivables beyond one year, so what is the actual ageing profile behind 124 debtor days?

verdict.our_read: A single-site Palghar generic formulations manufacturer that sells almost entirely into government tenders (Government Customers 89.93% of revenue from operations in the six months ended September 30, 2025, and 99.79% in Fiscal 2023), whose make-or-break tension is that profit has stopped converting into cash - PAT rose from Rs 222.50 million (Fiscal 2023) to Rs 412.66 million (Fiscal 2025) while cash flow from operations fell from Rs 332.85 million to Rs 107.67 million and trade receivables reached Rs 857.18 million, and the only quantified object of the Fresh Issue is Rs 725.00 million of working capital. Figures are in Rs million unless stated as lakhs.

parameter_scores.basis: Revenue from operations Rs 1,723.39 / 1,863.74 / 2,197.46 million; PAT Rs 222.50 / 341.38 / 412.66 million; EBITDA margin 17.81% / 23.66% / 24.52%; EPS Rs 4.46 / 6.85 / 8.28. Held back because the six months to September 30, 2025 show revenue of Rs 1,126.32 million and PAT of Rs 182.38 million with RoCE of 12.86% and RoNW of 9.71% as printed, and because the DRHP carries a second, internally inconsistent EBITDA series in Other Financial Information.

CFO Rs 332.85 / 198.91 / 107.67 million across Fiscals 2023-2025 while PAT rose from Rs 222.50 million to Rs 412.66 million; CFO Rs 68.04 million in the six months to September 30, 2025. Trade receivables Rs 450.91 / 493.43 / 673.20 / 857.18 million, at 76.10% of six-month revenue from operations; debtor days 97 / 92 / 97 / 124 against a stated 60-120 day realisation cycle; the Fiscal 2025 cash flow table itself sums to Rs -78.61 million against a printed Rs -78.63 million.

Total borrowings Rs 38.50 million at September 30, 2025, stated as 100% unsecured and being the interest-free promoter loan; net worth Rs 1,970.09 million; cash Rs 162.93 million; the Rs 150.00 million fund-based cash credit sub-limit entirely unutilised at November 30, 2025; nil pledge. Marked down only because that promoter loan is repayable on demand and Rs 328.37 million of tender bank guarantees sit off balance sheet.

Unit 1 in the six months to September 30, 2025 ran at 22.22% on tablets, 1.16% on capsules, 5.72% on sachets, 10.60% on syrups, 6.80% on external liquid, 0.40% on aerosol and 0.60% on external powder, with combi blister packs, kits and surgical dressing at nil production; tablets were 43.69% / 40.55% / 53.24% in the three Fiscals. Unit 2, at Rs 358.07 million of project cost and Rs 370.43 million of capital work-in-progress against net fixed assets of Rs 87.13 million, would add 2,500 million tablets of installed capacity on top of that.

No order book or unexecuted tender value is disclosed anywhere. Visibility rests on the bid pipeline: 22 of 28 bids won (78.57%) in the six months to September 30, 2025 with 20 awaiting results, against 55 of 86 (63.95%) and 59 of 99 (59.60%) in Fiscals 2025 and 2024, on contracts the DRHP describes as mostly one-time with no automatic renewal. Government Customers were 89.93% of revenue from operations in the latest period.

Largest customer 20.90% of revenue in the six months to September 30, 2025 against 13.38%, 11.74% and 15.00% in the three Fiscals; top 10 at 65.43% against 61.08% / 57.61% / 61.36%. Largest supplier moved 7.09% / 4.76% / 6.26% to 19.33% of cost of materials with no long-term supply contracts, top 10 suppliers to 50.48%. Blood-related, vitamin supplements, anti-infectives, cardiac and gastro-intestinal were 67.82% of revenue in the latest period against 53.06% in Fiscal 2025.

The single quantified object is Rs 725.00 million of working capital, with general corporate purposes unquantified and capped at 25% of Gross Proceeds; entire deployment scheduled in Fiscal 2027 and Nil in Fiscal 2026. Funding requirements have not been appraised by any bank or financial institution; a monitoring agency is stated to be appointed with quarterly reporting under Regulation 41. No plant or machinery object and no quotation annexure, so there is no un-ordered-capex exposure - but equally no asset is created, and the Rs 150.00 million cash credit line stood unused.
